content.value_statement: Real-time voice apps need reliable session, audio, and authentication patterns. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for Azure AI Voice Live in .NET.
actual_capabilities: Explains installing Azure.AI.VoiceLive, Azure.Identity, and NAudio packages.
Shows Entra ID and API key authentication patterns for VoiceLiveClient.
Outlines session setup with model, voice, modalities, and semantic VAD.
Describes handling audio, text, errors, and function call events.
Lists supported voices, model options, key SDK types, and reference links.
limitations: It does not run or validate Azure resources for the user.
It does not include a complete production audio pipeline or deployment plan.
Version details can change as Azure preview packages evolve.
Function calling examples require application-specific validation and permissions.

use_cases.title: Prototype Voice Assistants
use_cases.description: Build a quick Azure Voice Live proof of concept with session setup, audio formats, and event handling.

use_cases.title: Add Real-Time Audio
use_cases.description: Use the SDK patterns to add bidirectional voice features to an existing C# application.

use_cases.title: Plan Azure Integration
use_cases.description: Compare authentication options, models, voices, and related SDKs before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Voice Live Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a minimal .NET Azure AI Voice Live app. Include packages, authentication, endpoint setup, and session configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Conversation Audio
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through VoiceLiveSessionOptions for text and audio modalities. Use semantic VAD, PCM16 audio, and a standard Azure voice.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Streaming Events
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned Voice Live event loop. Cover audio deltas, text deltas, errors, response completion, and safe disposal.

prompt_templates.title: Design Function Calling
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a function calling flow for an Azure Voice Live assistant. Include schema design, argument validation, output handling, and permission boundaries.

output_examples.input: Create a Voice Live starter plan for a C# app.
output_examples.output: A setup plan covering NuGet packages, Azure endpoint configuration, DefaultAzureCredential, model choice, voice selection, and session lifecycle.

output_examples.input: Explain how to handle Voice Live updates.
output_examples.output: A review of audio delta playback, text streaming, function call handling, error handling, and response completion events.

output_examples.input: Compare SDK choices for realtime voice.
output_examples.output: A concise comparison of Azure.AI.VoiceLive, Speech SDK, and NAudio with when each package is useful.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential and managed access whenever possible.
Validate function call arguments before contacting external services.
Handle audio, text, error, and completion events in the session loop.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode API keys in source files or prompts.
Do not ignore session disposal, cancellation, or error events.
Do not assume preview model names or package versions stay stable.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build .NET apps that use Azure AI Voice Live for bidirectional voice interactions.

faq.question: Does it require an Azure account?
faq.answer: Yes. You need an Azure AI resource, endpoint, and either Entra ID access or an API key.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that need .NET guidance.

faq.question: Does it provide production-ready audio capture?
faq.answer: No. It references NAudio and PCM16 settings, but production audio handling needs separate testing.

faq.question: Does it support function calling?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains defining a Voice Live function, reading arguments, and returning function call output.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use environment variables or Azure identity. Avoid hardcoding API keys in code, prompts, or repository files.
